Description:

This role offers a hybrid opportunity, up to 2 days a week, after orientation period.**

Make a Meaningful Impact Beyond the Bedside!

Trinity Health IHA Medical Group is seeking a compassionate and patient-focused Care Manager - Oncology
to join our outpatient care team. In this role, you'll help patients navigate their healthcare journey through clinical triage, care coordination, patient education, and ongoing support that improves outcomes and enhances the patient experience.

What You'll Do:

Active member of the office based care team.
Provides care management, care coordination and navigation for patient beginning chemotherapy.
Assess and triage patient needs by phone and in-office visits.
Provide clinical guidance, patient education, and care coordination.
Support patients through transitions of care and post-discharge follow-up.
Collaborate with providers, care managers, pharmacists, behavioral health specialists, and other healthcare partners.
Manage medication refills, test results, referrals, and prior authorizations.
Identify preventive care needs and support chronic disease management.
Help patients access community resources and navigate barriers to care.
Serve as a clinical resource and leader within the care team.

What We're Looking For:

EDUCATION: Graduate of an accredited Registered Nurse program.
CREDENTIALS/LICENSURE: Valid, unrestricted RN license in the State of Michigan. Valid CPR certification. Prefer CCM/CCP certification.
MINIMUM EXPERIENCE: 3-5 years of clinical experience with oncology patients in primary care/ambulatory care, home health agency, skilled nursing facility, or hospital, within the past five years: knowledge of chronic conditions, evidence-based guidelines, prevention, wellness, health risk assessment, and patient education.

Why Join Trinity Health IHA Medical Group?

Day-one benefits with no waiting period for eligible colleagues.
Predictable outpatient schedule with a focus on work-life balance.
Collaborative team environment with strong provider partnerships.
Career growth, development, and advancement opportunities.
Meaningful work improving the health of patients and communities across Southeast Michigan.

About Us

At Trinity Health IHA Medical Group, we're committed to delivering exceptional care through our core values of Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, Efficiency, and Service. If you're passionate about patient-centered care and want to make a difference every day, we'd love to have you join our team.

Our Commitment

Rooted in our Mission and Core Values, we honor the dignity of every person and recognize the unique perspectives, experiences, and talents each colleague brings. By finding common ground and embracing our differences, we grow stronger together and deliver more compassionate, person-centered care. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager
jobs.description:
Manage Breakthrough Product Development Programs from Concept to Launch

Fieldpiece
is the innovation leader in professional HVACR test instruments, trusted by technicians around the world to solve some of the industry's toughest challenges. We're investing heavily in the future of product development through modern Fast Time To Market (FTTM) methodologies, connected products, AI-enabled engineering, and customer-centered innovation. Named one of the Best Places to Work in Southern California for four consecutive years
, we're looking for talented people who want to make an impact while growing their careers.

Why This Role?

Great products don't happen by accident - they happen because exceptional leaders bring people, ideas, and execution together.

As our Senior Program Manager
, you'll lead some of Fieldpiece's most strategic new product initiatives while helping transform how we develop products. You'll work across Engineering, Product Management, Industrial Design, Quality, Manufacturing, and global development partners to align teams, remove obstacles, and deliver innovative connected products.

Beyond delivering successful programs, you'll play a key role in advancing our FTTM methodology, helping us continuously improve how we innovate, collaborate, and bring products to market. If you enjoy solving complex challenges, influencing without authority, and turning ambitious ideas into reality, you'll thrive in this role.

This position is in our Orange, CA office with an exciting move to Tustin, CA in 2028.
This role follows a hybrid work schedule
, with employees typically working onsite three days per week. Additional in-office days may be required from time to time for onboarding, training, team meetings, project collaboration, or other business needs.

What You'll Do

Lead multiple, complex new product development programs from concept through commercial launch that include hardware, firmware, and software.
Align cross-functional teams across Product Management, Engineering, Industrial Design, Quality, Operations, and Manufacturing.
Drive program planning, risk management, executive communication, and decision-making.
Coordinate global development activities with suppliers and strategic partners.
Champion Fast Time To Market (FTTM) methodologies and continuous improvement.
Help build a culture of accountability, transparency, and excellence in execution.

What Makes This Opportunity Different

You'll help redefine how an entire company develops products while bringing innovative connected technologies to market faster than ever before.
Shape the future of product development at an innovation-driven company building the next-generation of connected HVACR products by applying FTTM methodologies to accelerate innovation.
Influence both what we build to solve real customer problems and how we build them.
Help drive the adoption of AI-enabled engineering, connected products, and technician productivity solutions in collaboration with global engineering organizations and strategic technology partners.

In Your First Year, You'll Likely Have

Successfully lead multiple new product development programs through key development milestones.
Become a trusted cross-functional leader who helps teams make better, faster decisions.
Embedded FTTM best practices into day-to-day program execution.
Built strong relationships with internal teams and strategic external partners.
Improved program visibility, risk management, and execution predictability.

Qualifications

What You Bring:

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, or a related STEM field.
10+ years of program and/or project management experience leading complex new product development initiatives in engineering or manufacturing environments.
A proven track record managing multiple concurrent projects and integrated product programs, aligning cross-functional teams to deliver on schedule.
Experience leading hardware, firmware, and software product development programs from concept through launch.
Strong understanding of the product development lifecycle, including both hardware development and software development processes.
Experience working with global suppliers, ODMs, contract manufacturers, and overseas manufacturing partners.
Proficiency with project management and collaboration tools, including Microsoft Office and modern project tracking software.

Bonus Points If You Have

Experience establishing or improving project governance, stage-gate reviews, PMO structures, or organizational change within a growing or rapidly scaling company.
Experience with Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or Microsoft Project.
Professional certifications such as PMP, Prosci, Lean Six Sigma, or similar.
Experience helping organizations improve program execution through modern product development methodologies.

Why You'll Enjoy Working at Fieldpiece

As a privately held company, we invest for the long term—in our people, our products, and our future. That means we can focus on innovation, continuous improvement, and building lasting careers rather than chasing short-term results.
Work alongside talented, collaborative teammates who are passionate about innovation and solving real world problems.
Make a meaningful impact in a company where your ideas are heard, your expertise is valued, and your contributions help shape the future of our products and business.

Benefits & Perks

We believe great work starts with supporting our employees. That's why we offer a competitive total rewards package designed to promote your health, financial well-being, work-life balance, and professional growth.

Competitive base salary with annual bonus opportunity
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
401(k) with company match and immediate vesting
Generous paid time off and paid holidays
Hire to Retire philosophy - Individual Development Plans for everyone and a commitment to support career development
Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), Health Savings Accounts (HSA), and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Music program – music rooms in all US offices with onsite guitar, piano, and voice lessons in California (classes can be streamed for other offices)
Recognition programs, launch parties and team building events to share successes

Our Culture

At Fieldpiece, our values shape how we work, collaborate, and serve our customers every day. We believe in:

Teamwork – We collaborate, support one another, and win as a team.
Urgency – We move quickly, stay agile, and focus on what matters most.
Respect – We value diverse perspectives and treat everyone with professionalism and integrity.
Trust – We build strong relationships through accountability and transparency.
Learning – We embrace curiosity, continuous improvement, and personal growth.
No Ego – We leave titles and egos at the door, value the best ideas regardless of where they come from, and work together with humility, openness, and mutual respect.

jobs.title: RN Case Manager
jobs.description:
At St. Croix Hospice, we believe in the power of compassionate care. Like the river that inspired our name and takes great skill to navigate, St. Croix Hospice guides patients and their families through the end-of-life journey. We are committed to ensuring the highest quality of life for our patients, empowering them to make the most of their time with dignity, comfort and respect. If you are ready to be part of our deeply compassionate family of caregivers guiding extraordinary life experiences, then we invite you to join our team, where your work truly matters.

In the role of Registered Nurse Case Manager
, you’ll be entrusted with providing 1:1, whole-person care to patients and families in their homes. Partnering with an integrated care team, you will coordinate individualized care plans, support families through complex decisions, and offer comfort with professionalism, empathy, and respect.

If you're a compassionate Registered Nurse who values meaningful patient connections and autonomy in your practice, we’d love to meet you.

Qualifications

Registered Nurse Case Manager Requirements & Responsibilities:

Associates, Bachelors, or Masters of an accredited nursing program (RN)
1+ years of recent acute care experience required; hospice/home health experience preferred
Complete initial and ongoing comprehensive assessments to determine hospice needs
Develop individualized care plans with the patient and family, updating as needs evolve
Administer medications and treatments as prescribed
Educate patients and caregivers on care techniques, medications, diet, and symptom management
Rotate on-call duties and ensure seamless care transitions
Must have reliable transportation, valid driver’s license, and proof of auto insurance

Benefits & Schedule:

Schedule: 8:00am to 5:00pm, Full-time position with on-call expectations
Health, dental, vision, and life insurance
Company-paid short/long-term disability and basic life insurance
401(k) with up to 4% company match
Tuition reimbursement and professional development opportunities
Paid time off and paid holidays

jobs.description:
#15654

Lincoln, Nebraska, USA

Full-Time/Part-Time

Full-time

Job Description

About AEG:

At AEG, we're building something bigger than great eye care, we're creating careers, developing leaders, and making a meaningful difference in the communities we serve.

You'll Join a Team That

Invests in leadership development and internal growth.
Believes people and performance go hand in hand.
Values collaboration, authenticity, and continuous learning.
Celebrates wins, supports challenges, and grows together.

About The Role

At AEG, we believe great patient experiences begin with great teams. As a Patient Care Coordinator you are responsible not only for front desk operations, but also for supporting patient flow, schedule optimization, and seamless coordination across the care team.

The ability to anticipate needs, communicate clearly, and proactively manage the daily schedule helps ensure an efficient, high-quality experience for every patient.

Greet patients, customers, and vendors in a friendly, professional, and welcoming manner; serve as the primary point of contact for patient interactions.
Answer telephone calls, respond to inquiries, and manage email or digital communications in a timely and professional manner.
Schedule patient appointments while supporting provider schedule optimization, including managing cancellations, reschedules, and same-day fill opportunities.
Execute appointment confirmation and reminder processes to reduce no-show rates and ensure patients are prepared for their visit.
Verify insurance eligibility and patient demographics prior to appointments; accurately enter and maintain complete information in EMR.
Maintain a clear understanding of insurance plans and effectively communicate coverage, benefits, and patient financial responsibility.
Prepare patient charts and required documentation in advance of visits to support efficient patient flow.
Collect and document all charges, co-pays, and payments into EMR; allocate balances appropriately and support claim preparation and submission.
Run reports and review accounts to ensure all charges are billed, filed, and up to date.
Monitor daily patient flow and provider schedules to identify bottlenecks, delays, or overlaps; communicate and adjust as needed to support efficient patient flow.
Proactively communicate with patients regarding wait times, delays, and next steps to maintain a positive experience.
Coordinate with clinical and optical teams to ensure smooth patient transitions and continuity of care throughout the visit.
Support patient retention efforts through follow-up, recall, and reactivation outreach, including annual and medically necessary appointments.
Assist in maintaining an organized, clean, and patient-ready front office environment.
Perform other duties as needed and as assigned by the Practice Manager, Assistant Practice Manager and/or Optometrist.

Requirements

High school diploma or equivalent.
Basic computer literacy and ability to learn practice management systems (EMR).
Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities.
Strong communication skills (verbal and written) with a focus on patient-centered service.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively across teams.
Ability to proactively identify issues and contribute to solutions in a fast-paced environment.
Must be able to maintain patient and practice confidentiality.

Full Time Employee Benefits

401(k) with Match
Medical/Dental/Vision/Life/STD/LTD
Employee Vision Discount Program
HSA/FSA
PTO
Paid Holidays

Physical Demands

Ability to utilize office equipment
Prolonged sitting, standing, and walking
Ability to lift up to 10 lbs

Current CNA certification.
Experience in home care, senior care, assisted living, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, or a similar setting.
Experience with dementia and Alzheimer's care.
Strong experience with transfers, gait belts, mobility assistance, and fall prevention.
Experience safely using Hoyer lifts and other transfer equipment.
Experience with bathing, dressing, toileting, personal care, and activities of daily living.
Previous experience training, mentoring, supervising, or leading caregivers is strongly preferred.

About Ascendion

Ascendion is an AI-native software engineering disruptor helping businesses innovate faster, smarter, and with greater impact. We partner with enterprise clients across North America, the UK, Europe, and APAC to solve complex challenges in data, experience design, software product engineering, and workforce transformation. Powered by expert engineers, thousands of AI agents, and our Engineering to the Power of AI (EngineeringAI) method, we deliver measurable outcomes that build trust, unlock value, and accelerate growth.
Learn more at  https://ascendion.com/.
Engineering to the Power of AI™, AAVA™, EngineeringAI, Engineering to Elevate Life™, Enterprise PlatformsAI, Data & InsightsAI, ExperienceAI, GCCAI, OperationsAI, Platform EngineeringAI, ProductAI, and Quality EngineeringAI are trademarks or service marks of Ascendion®. AAVA™ is pending registration. Unauthorized use is strictly prohibited.
Ascendion | Engineering to elevate life

We have a culture built on opportunity, inclusion, and a spirit of partnership. Come, change the world with us:
Build the coolest tech for the world’s leading brands
Solve complex problems - and learn new skills
Experience the power of transforming digital engineering for Fortune 500 clients
Master your craft with leading training programs and hands-on experience

Experience a community of change makers!

Join a culture of high-performing innovators with endless ideas and a passion for tech. Our culture is the fabric of our company, and it is what makes us unique and diverse. The way we share ideas, learning, experiences, successes, and joy allows everyone to be their best at Ascendion.
About the Role:

We are seeking a Program Manager to support the Energy and Sustainability organization’s clean energy strategy and the reporting that underpins Net Zero commitments.
The role will serve as the day-to-day owner and coordinator for energy activity data — the Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 energy datasets that feed the company's greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory, emissions forecasting, and voluntary and regulatory disclosures.
This is a hands-on, data-centric role requiring 3-5 years of experience managing multiple concurrent workstreams in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, direct experience working with large datasets and running or Quality Checking (QC'ing) analytics, and the ability to communicate data status and insights to technical and non-technical audiences.
The individual must have familiarity with corporate GHG accounting and be comfortable with query tools and data Quality Assurance (QA)/validation workflows.

Job Title:
Sustainability Program Manager II
Minimum Qualifications:

BA or BS degree in physical sciences, engineering, math, statistics, accounting, business, environment, and/or a sustainability-focused field.
3-5 years of experience in program management, data operations, or analytics coordination, ideally supporting technical or data-oriented teams.
Direct, hands-on experience working with large datasets — collecting, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), reconciling, and analyzing data from multiple sources.
Familiarity with corporate Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions accounting concepts (Scope 1, 2, and 3) and the activity data that underpins an emissions inventory.
Exceptional project-management skills with a demonstrated ability to self-manage complex, data-driven delivery in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting data and insights to technical and non-technical audiences and creating graphics for leadership presentations.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data work, even under tight deadlines.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment and comfort with ambiguity.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with a scripting/query language (e.g., Structured Query Language (SQL), Python) sufficient to run, automate, or Quality Assurance (QA) data pulls from large data warehouses (e.g., Hive/Presto or equivalent).
Experience building visualizations and dashboards from large, multi-source datasets, particularly with Tableau and Excel.
Familiarity with energy/utility data (electricity, natural gas, diesel, and other fuels) and metering/billing data structures.
Strong understanding of current practices and trends in greenhouse gas emissions and broader sustainability accounting and reporting.
Familiarity with external reporting standards and platforms such as Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP), Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), etc.
Experience supporting external assurance or audit processes.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as the day-to-day owner for energy activity data across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 electricity (e.g., FERA, construction energy, network-related electricity, and operational electricity, diesel, natural gas, etc.), from data collection and Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) through to the reporting handoff to the Net Zero team.
Perform analyses on the Environmental Attribute Certificate (EAC) portfolio and support the development of internal systems to advance portfolio management and modeling.
Run and maintain the recurring data collection, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), and validation cadence (e.g., quarterly data pulls, follow-ups, Year-over-Year (YoY) analysis) and keep reporting and analysis on schedule.
Perform and Quality Check (QC) data pulls from energy data systems, investigate anomalies and data-pipeline issues, and reconcile discrepancies.
Coordinate data and process flows across cross-functional partners to maintain accurate and complete inputs from source through to reporting.
Support the emissions forecasting cadence as the energy-data point of contact for the Net Zero team, providing and Quality Assuring (QA'ing) the activity data behind regulatory and internal cross-functional forecasts.
Develop and maintain program-management artifacts — trackers, roadmaps, status reports, and executive-ready updates — for recurring leadership and cross-functional forums.
Support a quarterly reporting cadence (execution updates, executive meeting preparation, deck and dashboard creation) using established templates and inputs.
Support external assurance and audit activities (e.g., methodology walkthroughs with the assurance provider) and prepare and validate data and documentation as requested.
Triage and respond to incoming energy-data and analytical requests; track progress against internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and stakeholder expectations.
Maintain and improve reporting documentation — the what, when, where, how, and why of energy data collection, including team-specific nuances and process flows.

Location:
 Remote [USA ONLY]

Salary Range: 
The salary for this position is between $116,400 - $166,400 annually.  Factors which may affect pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Program Manager to support the Energy and Sustainability organization’s clean energy strategy and the reporting that underpins Net Zero commitments.
The role will serve as the day-to-day owner and coordinator for energy activity data — the Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 energy datasets that feed the company's greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory, emissions forecasting, and voluntary and regulatory disclosures.
This is a hands-on, data-centric role requiring 3-5 years of experience managing multiple concurrent workstreams in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, direct experience working with large datasets and running or Quality Checking (QC'ing) analytics, and the ability to communicate data status and insights to technical and non-technical audiences.
The individual must have familiarity with corporate GHG accounting and be comfortable with query tools and data Quality Assurance (QA)/validation workflows.

Job Title:
Sustainability Program Manager II
Minimum Qualifications:

BA or BS degree in physical sciences, engineering, math, statistics, accounting, business, environment, and/or a sustainability-focused field.
3-5 years of experience in program management, data operations, or analytics coordination, ideally supporting technical or data-oriented teams.
Direct, hands-on experience working with large datasets — collecting, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), reconciling, and analyzing data from multiple sources.
Familiarity with corporate Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions accounting concepts (Scope 1, 2, and 3) and the activity data that underpins an emissions inventory.
Exceptional project-management skills with a demonstrated ability to self-manage complex, data-driven delivery in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting data and insights to technical and non-technical audiences and creating graphics for leadership presentations.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data work, even under tight deadlines.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment and comfort with ambiguity.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with a scripting/query language (e.g., Structured Query Language (SQL), Python) sufficient to run, automate, or Quality Assurance (QA) data pulls from large data warehouses (e.g., Hive/Presto or equivalent).
Experience building visualizations and dashboards from large, multi-source datasets, particularly with Tableau and Excel.
Familiarity with energy/utility data (electricity, natural gas, diesel, and other fuels) and metering/billing data structures.
Strong understanding of current practices and trends in greenhouse gas emissions and broader sustainability accounting and reporting.
Familiarity with external reporting standards and platforms such as Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP), Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), etc.
Experience supporting external assurance or audit processes.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as the day-to-day owner for energy activity data across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 electricity (e.g., FERA, construction energy, network-related electricity, and operational electricity, diesel, natural gas, etc.), from data collection and Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) through to the reporting handoff to the Net Zero team.
Perform analyses on the Environmental Attribute Certificate (EAC) portfolio and support the development of internal systems to advance portfolio management and modeling.
Run and maintain the recurring data collection, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), and validation cadence (e.g., quarterly data pulls, follow-ups, Year-over-Year (YoY) analysis) and keep reporting and analysis on schedule.
Perform and Quality Check (QC) data pulls from energy data systems, investigate anomalies and data-pipeline issues, and reconcile discrepancies.
Coordinate data and process flows across cross-functional partners to maintain accurate and complete inputs from source through to reporting.
Support the emissions forecasting cadence as the energy-data point of contact for the Net Zero team, providing and Quality Assuring (QA'ing) the activity data behind regulatory and internal cross-functional forecasts.
Develop and maintain program-management artifacts — trackers, roadmaps, status reports, and executive-ready updates — for recurring leadership and cross-functional forums.
Support a quarterly reporting cadence (execution updates, executive meeting preparation, deck and dashboard creation) using established templates and inputs.
Support external assurance and audit activities (e.g., methodology walkthroughs with the assurance provider) and prepare and validate data and documentation as requested.
Triage and respond to incoming energy-data and analytical requests; track progress against internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and stakeholder expectations.
Maintain and improve reporting documentation — the what, when, where, how, and why of energy data collection, including team-specific nuances and process flows.
